summary: This bill amends the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 to allow federal community development block grant funds to be used by metropolitan cities, urban counties, states, local governments, insular areas, or tribal entities for the construction of new residential housing for low- and moderate-income individuals.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands the eligible uses of existing Housing and Community Development Act funds to include the construction of new residential housing for low- and moderate-income persons. While it doesn't directly appropriate new funds, it directs how existing or future allocated funds can be spent, potentially leading to increased spending on housing construction within the existing program framework.

By allowing Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds to be used for the construction of new residential housing for low- and moderate-income persons, the bill aims to increase the availability of affordable housing. This expansion of housing options for vulnerable populations directly strengthens a component of the social safety net.
